title: The Mysterious Matter of Antimatter
paragraphs: The world that humans commonly interact with is comprised of ordinary matter. Such matter consists of atomic particles like protons, electrons, neutrons, and (presumably) neutrinos. A common debate in science surrounds the question of dark matter, which is observed to influence gravitational behavior at galactic scales. It is often questioned whether dark matter should be considered “matter” at all. Though, a mystery that often goes overlooked concerns a different type of matter: antimatter. Antimatter has been proven to exist via various experiments with particle colliders. Based upon current models, ordinary matter should exist in a universe with an equal amount of antimatter. Yet, current astronomical tools detect much less antimatter throughout the universe than current models predict.
The Universe's Dark Secret: Where Did All the Antimatter Go? | Space

Antimatter is an incredibly interesting phenomenon. The mass of an antimatter particle is identical to its normal matter counterpart. Though, the charge is often equal and opposite (1). For example, positrons have the same mass as electrons, but the charges are different. Electrons have a negative charge, whereas antielectrons have a positive charge. Additionally, a lepton or baryon number is assigned to antimatter particle that is opposite to that of a matter particle. Positrons are given a lepton number of -1, whereas electrons are given the lepton number of +1. In the case of a neutron, which always has a neutral charge, an antineutron has the same “charge” and merely carries an opposite baryon number. Interestingly, antimatter also exists among all known fundamental particles, including exotic particles like a muon or a tau (1). When matter and antimatter interact, it is explosive and often results in photonic energy being emitted. Going back to the electron and antielectron, they tend to emit two photons when they collide. Granted, higher energy collisions can yield different particles than just photons.

Despite much being known about antimatter behavior, the observed amount of antimatter defies expectation. Due to interactions between matter and antimatter being highly energetic, astronomical activity is of a much lower energy than expectation (2). This immense asymmetry defies what many might expect. Several explanations have been proposed. One possibility is that antimatter dominates a distant and unobservable portion of space, which is essentially lost to the portion of the universe that consists of matter (3). If the force of gravity can be described on quantum scales, it could also be that antimatter dominated regions of space follow different rules of gravity, in the form of “antigravity” (3). This could facilitate the matter/antimatter disconnect.

The leading explanation for matter and antimatter disparity comes from CERN. There was an observed 1% difference in the decay of muons vs antimuons from mesons. Such a difference in decay rates could have led matter to dominate at the inception of the universe. Therefore, the observable matter in the universe could very well just be the 1% of matter that remains from antiparticle and particle interactions. While this explanation is satisfying, there is still skepticism to be had. Antimatter and matter interactions outlined by the standard model and the simplest Feynman diagram models could lead one to believe that there should be no difference in percentages. A 1% difference can also be accounted for by an overlooked experimental error in the particle accelerator. Furthermore, only so many experiments have been carried out. That said, when one considers that there are always quantum probabilities involved in particle/antiparticle interactions (Feynman diagrams even acknowledge this), a random cosmic coin flip could in fact explain the mystery.

The universe contains countless secrets, which are still yet to be uncovered. While questions of our universe’s antimatter and matter is still up in the air, there are at least very real and reproducible explanations. Here is hoping that an explanation is cemented over the coming years.

title: A New Phase of Matter: The Power of Quantum Computing
paragraphs: Matter is commonly understood to exist in three phases: liquid, gas, and solid. However, there are many unique phases of matter that can be distinguished beyond these three. Among these are plasmas, Bose-Einstein Condensates, and mesophases. The processes of quantum computing have enabled computer scientists to identify a new phase of matter. More precisely, they have discovered a new kind of “topological phase” (1). Additionally, their phase is claimed to feature symmetry across an extra time dimension (1).

A topological phase is a bit different from the conventional phases of matter. Namely, it is not defined by interatomic structure or atomic arrangement. Instead, topological phases are defined by the interatomic interactions and motions (1). Distinct phases are usually created by inducing a synchronicity, or “symmetry”, in atomic motions (2). These are induced via electromagnetically, such as through laser pulses. Interestingly, when inducing repetitive motions among vast quantities of atoms, they do not need to be symmetrical through physical space (1). Rather, their physics only need to be symmetrical across two time dimensions.

The method of using laser pulses was the choice of research physicists at the Flatiron Institute. They were experimenting with pulses toward charged ions in a quantum computer. The breakthrough for the researchers occurred when trying to create a laser pulse sequence that did not repeat any numbers, but still had an internal order. The goal was to imbue their material with the features of quasicrystals, due to them being able to retain shape when pushed through “higher dimensions” (2). This was important for creating symmetry through time. Thus, their choice was to utilize the Fibonacci sequence (3). They replicated this sequence by sending two laser pulses at different frequencies, with the pattern of “A, AB, ABA, ABAAB, ABAABABA…” (1).

The hope of the researchers is to use their new discovery to insulate quantum computers from seeing errors. This application is especially important for quantum computers, as they do not operate on the binary logic of classical computing. Rather, they rely on quantum electron spin of qubits. This can exist in the three states of up, down, or a superposition of both. The quantum nature of quantum computers makes them especially susceptible to failures from electromagnetic noise (3). According to the researchers though, “In a quantum computer that exploits topology, information is not encoded locally in the state of each qubit but is woven across the material globally” (1). Such a method would insulate from any simple noise errors. Due to rapid development in quantum computing research, researchers on this quantum structuring will hopefully find success. Error-free quantum computing would allow for massive strides throughout a variety of fields. Furthermore, the field of quantum computing itself continues to yield exciting prospects.

title: NASA Space Probe Touches the Sun
paragraphs: Space probes proliferate the Solar System, exploring various incredible areas. However, an area of the Solar System that has gone largely untapped is the Solar System’s own namesake — the Sun. That is, up until recently. A new NASA space probe, dubbed the “Parker Probe”, has just touched the Sun’s corona. This is truly a feat of science and engineering.
How did NASA's probe touch the Sun without melting? NASA answers | TweakTown

The reason that the Parker Probe can withstand the Sun’s heat has everything to do with its design. On the most fundamental levels, the Parker Probe’s technology is engineered for the task. It is retrofitted with white, reflective solar shields, which reorient themselves to redirect the Sun’s heat (1). The orientation of the solar shield is monitored by an on-board solar sensor, which can detect the direction of the Sun’s energy. It accomplishes this by measuring photon wavelengths — the intensity of light (2).

In addition to its solar shielding, the probe has a water-cooling system and radiator (1). These do a lot of heavy lifting in terms of keeping the system from overheating. Nevertheless, the conditions that the Parker Probe must endure are quite extreme. Its sensors, which have minimal shielding, endure temperatures of 1,000 degrees Celsius (2). To reduce damage of the machine, it is constructed of high-grade materials with high melting points: “tungsten, niobium, molybdenum, and sapphire” (2).

The mission of the Parker Probe is to gather new data on the behavior within the Sun’s corona. This area of the Sun is dominated by magnetic fields and solar winds, which can impact our electronics on Earth. Thus far, the probe has been able to determine patterns in solar winds, and where they originate (3). However, another thing the probe is trying to uncover is why the Sun’s atmosphere is so much hotter than its surface (2). It has been studying the boundary between the solar atmosphere and solar winds and found them to be “wrinkled rather than smooth” (3). NASA appears to be happy with their results, reporting, “We see evidence of being in the corona in magnetic field data, solar wind data, and visually in images. We can actually see the spacecraft flying through coronal structures that can be observed during a total solar eclipse” (2).

The Parker Probe is yet another feat of NASA innovation that stands as a reminder of what can be achieved through technology. The science it is uncovering is helping massively in the construction of better scientific models for star behavior. Hopefully the Parker Probe will continue to make new findings and give us a clearer picture of our universe.

title: What Are Semiconductors?
paragraphs: The world of the 21st century has been defined by rapid advances in software and computing technology. Much credit is given to Moore’s Law, where we see a doubling in transistor density among new computers each year. However, a critical component that is often overlooked is the advancement in material science that brought us modern computing: semiconductors. Semiconductors are a special material that enables our computer circuits to function. Without the key advancement of semiconductors, much of our electronic technology would not be able to exist.
How Semiconductors Work (lifewire.com)

Usage of semiconductor materials are widespread, being built into, “integrated circuits, microchips, transistors, and many sensors” (1). The materials used to create semiconductors are also quite varied: silicon, germanium, gallium arsenide, and silicon carbide are just a few of the materials used (1). Silicon is the most common semiconductor, due to it being quite abundant. If you go to a beach that is covered with sand, you are looking at a wealth of silicon. Regardless of semiconductor material, the appeal of semiconductors is that their electrical conductivity polarity can easily be manipulated. The variation in semiconductor electric current is core to creating any kind of logic-processing system.

The reason why elements like silicon, carbon, and germanium are ideal semiconductors is due to their electron orbitals. Each of these materials have 4 electrons, which make them great at forming covalent bonds with crystal structures (2). Unlike the free electron clouds of metallic bonds, the electrons in crystal covalent bonds are practically locked in place (2). They act as insulators that do not conduct electric current. However, these insulative materials can be “doped” with structural impurities by other materials, to be able to conduct some electrons (2). This is how these nonconductive insulators can become semiconductors.

When an insulator like silicon is doped with phosphorous or arsenic, which have five electrons, a free electron becomes present in silicon’s crystal lattices (3). Thus, silicon becomes negatively charged when conducting electricity, and is known as an “N-type” semiconductor (3). If silicon is doped with boron or gallium, which have three electrons, there is a gap of an electron in the silicon lattices. Thus, the lattices become positively charged when conducting electricity, and are known as a “P-type” semiconductor (3).  Combining these types of semiconductors in various ways allows for unique circuit behavior.
How Semiconductors Work | HowStuffWorks

The simplest example of a semiconductor circuit is a diode, such as in the image above. When a P-type and N-type semiconductor are combined in sequence, electricity from a battery will only flow in one direction — from positive to negative (3). This is due to the polarity of the charges in the semiconductor materials. If a battery is reversed in its placement, with positive-to-positive and negative-to-negative? Electricity will not be able to flow, due to the electron charges repelling one another. Such a device is incredibly useful and can protect devices from being damaged by something like a misplaced battery (3).

In addition to diodes, semiconductors can also be used to create transistors. These are formed via NPN and PNP semiconductor sandwiches (3). While a large current cannot normally flow straight through a semiconductor sandwich, due to the opposing polarities? If a small current is pushed through the center of the semiconductor sandwich, the polarity of the sandwich can be changed to PPP or NNN — thus, allowing a large current to flow (3). This allows for switching functions — otherwise known as binary “1s and 0s” — which is a fundamental concept to designing machines that can process logic. Without it, computers would not exist.

Electronic technologies today are heavily dependent upon the science of semiconductors. Over the years semiconductor chemistries have been refined, allowing for electronic devices that can hold thousands upon thousands of logic transistors within their circuits.  Moreover, simpler technologies like LED lights or microwaves are also reliant upon semiconductors. The science of semiconductors is incredibly interesting, and the world they have provided us is even more so.

title: EAST Fusion Reactor: Five Times Hotter than the Sun
paragraphs: The race for fusion energy is heating up. Literally. China has successfully begun experiments on its fusion reactor, the Experimental Advanced Superconducting Tokomak (EAST). The results have been reaffirming to the initiative of fusion. Should they continue to see these promising results, fusion may have a viable future that is nearer than many have thought.
China switched on its nuclear fusion device that’s 5 times hotter than the Sun (yahoo.com)

Fusion involves fusing two atoms together, to release energy. It is the process that stars undergo in their cores, to generate plasma. Down here on Earth, fusion involves fusing two hydrogen atoms together into helium plasma (1), via reactors that can generate high heats and pressures. This form of energy is especially appealing, due to its lack of harmful waste, lack of risk for meltdown, and the abundance of hydrogen fuel. It has the potential to become the cleanest and most energy dense form of energy production (for a more detailed look into fusion reactor science, see here: Fusion and its Future).

The EAST has been a long and hard effort, having taken a trillion dollars and years to build. During the EAST’s recent tests, it became clear that the investment paid off. The EAST shattered previous fusion records, running for a full 17 minutes at 70 million degrees Celsius (2). For perspective, these temperatures were at five times hotter than the Sun (2). Data retrieved from this experiment and EAST’s subsequent experiments, will give key insight into future reactor designs. The hope is for scientists to develop fusion reactors that can achieve ignition and truly withstand the intense plasma conditions, over extensive periods of time.

EAST only marks the beginning of potential in fusion development. The teams that worked on EAST are also working on the ITER, in France (1). The ITER is to be the biggest and most powerful fusion reactor ever built (1). This global effort toward fusion is inspiring, on all fronts. Should the sustainable energy resource of fusion be achieved, it would be a massive gamechanger on a global scale.

title: Radio Transmission: How Does it Work?
paragraphs: Radio waves permeate our universe, and radio technology is used all throughout our daily lives. Moreover, radio technologies were essential in the developmental stages of our current communication technologies. Nevertheless, the science behind the transmission of radio waves often goes untouched. Let’s look a bit into what radio waves are, and how radio transmission operates.
Radio Waves | Science Mission Directorate (nasa.gov)

Radio waves are a form of electromagnetic energy along the electromagnetic spectrum. Specifically, they are among the longest wavelengths of electromagnetic energy. The radio wave was first discovered in the 1880s by Heinrich Hertz. He was doing an experiment with a high-voltage spark gap connected to an induction coil, and a second spark gap connected to a wire antenna (1).  When he sent electricity through his first spark gap and induction coil, Hertz saw something interesting. A second spark occurred a bit away, within the second spark gap that was connected to his antenna (1).

Since Hertz’s discovery, subsequent experiments modeled out the behavior of radio waves (1). It was realized that radio waves’ long electromagnetic wavelength allows them to transmit low amounts of energy over long distances. Furthermore, such energy could be used as a way of transmitting information and data. It is for this reason that the “frequency” of radio waves — the number of wave cycles per second (2) — bear the name “hertz”.
Bandwidth, Frequency and Data Rate | Home (ad-net.com.tw)

Radio waves are produced any time that a flow of electrons, or electric current, is formed. They can be generated by something as simple as intermittently shorting the terminals of a 9-volt battery with a piece of metal (2). These quick changes in electric current, or “pulse modulations”, will induce a magnetic field in the air. This causes the formation of electromagnetic radio waves (2).  While such a simple signal can only be read as random static by a wire antenna, more advanced circuitry turns radio waves into a very useful tool.

In commercial radio transmitters, several electric components are used to enhance and modulate electric radio wave signals. These components include capacitors, resistors, inductors, transistors, and antenna wires (2). Capacitors store and release large capacities of electric charge, via storing large amounts of electrons between a dielectric material. Resistors use resistive metals, to slow down electric currents. Inductors use magnetic fields to induce stronger electric currents. Transistors allow for quick transitions in “voltage”, otherwise known as electric potential energy difference. Transistors are what help produce organized radio waveforms. Antenna wires provide terminals between a radio transmitter and radio receiver (2). Out of all these components, the transistor may be the most important. The organized waveforms created by transistors allow radio waves to be translated and amplified into logical signals by radio receivers (2), such as sound.
Simple and Quick FM Transmitter - DIY (circuits-diy.com)

Radio waves are transformed in a variety of ways while being transmitted and received. This is so that many waves can travel long distances, without getting tangled with one another (4). The two most common ways of radio transformation are frequency modulation (FM) and amplitude modulation (AM). In frequency modulation, the frequency of a radio wave is shifted (2). Shifting frequency involves changing the rate of a radio wave’s cycles per second. Amplitude modulation involves shifting the amplitude. Amplitude modulation changes the peak voltage of a radio wave signal. Radio transmitters are often where the modulation of radio waves is performed (5). Radio receivers are then tuned to the desired FM or AM channel, where they will convert a modulated radio signal back into their original forms (5).
How Radio Works | HowStuffWorks

Radio technologies are visibly present in our day-to-day activities, but the underlying theories to them remain quite invisible to the naked eye. Even in this article, we have only scratched the surface of the subject. Simply put, radios are complex. Despite this, they are well worth learning about. The depth of science involved in the innocuous radio serves as a reminder: never stop being curious about the technologies encompassing the world around us.

title: DevOp Engineer: The Most In-Demand Software Developmental Team Role
paragraphs: While system administration, programmers, and developers can all work on the same project under the same roof, there is not necessarily a seamless flow of communication and work between these parties. This division of labor is painful and can harm the effectiveness of the product. Users of the 21st century expect applications that are constantly getting better and more efficient. A DevOp is the clear and modern solution, for organizations with 20/20 vision. In this article, we will go over the fundamentals of what a DevOp is, how a DevOp can benefit your product, and the qualities of DevOps.
What is DevOps? DevOps Explained | Microsoft Azure

People often wonder: what Is a DevOp? A DevOp is the merging of development and operations. It ultimately makes software development, upgrading, and release as seamless as possible (1). DevOps reduce the complexity of these processes, closing the gap between new application development and current application reliability. These talented individuals are constantly adding to their skill sets on top of previous experience to offer a broader hand to the project.

A good DevOp will be able to combine application development aspects like library updates or data organization with foundational communication and coordination skills. This cultivates a beautiful, holistic flow within software development. You might call a DevOp the glue that binds the software engineering and IT of a project together. Continuous integration, as well as continuous delivery, make the DevOp a unique role. While traditional software engineering works in linear stages, DevOp engineering runs an ongoing feedback loop to maintain flawless flow (1). Through automation, this loop of unification is made up of development life processes like coding and deployment maintenance.

The introduction of new tools and methods makes a DevOp the ultimate integrative engineer, combining management, application stability, and code. An especially valuable skill that DevOps bring to the Software Development Team is improving and redesigning IT infrastructure (1). Sluggishness in a team’s core infrastructure might obstruct a software’s full potential. The improvements and redesigns a of a DevOp improve collaboration, allowing releases to come out quicker.

DevOps automate crucial, yet repetitive and time consuming tasks. A DevOp can create software plugins that lighten the software team’s workload, so they can spend energy on bigger things (2). They also manage IT Projects. This allows DevOps to designate the when, where, how, who and what of IT projects, crucial to your software.  In this way, DevOps determine the reliability of current software developments.
What Is DevOps? The Ultimate Guide (techtarget.com)

Another DevOp ability is evaluating system and software reliability, through performance testing and benchmark efforts. This is indispensable. Adding to this valuable ability is their creation of SecDevOps. SecDevOps are security processes, crucial to DevOp organized processes (2). These include schedules, automation, and infrastructure design. Another way SecDevOps help is by monitoring and providing feedback on TTD and TTM TTD (time to detect errors), and TTM (time to minimize errors). This removes hidden drains in the software release process.

A DevOp optimizes release cycles, so new releases can get to the market faster. One of the main tools a DevOp uses to do this is automation. As a result of their work, releasing frequently is easy. DevOps deploy releases many times a day, without users ever noticing. Thus, your software development and IT teams have more time and energy to focus on creativity, modification, upgrades, and groundbreaking improvements or changes. Various IT Functions and developmental strands can also work coherently with a DevOp. Each new and unique bit of development will build on top of the other, to create a coherent experience for the user.

A good DevOp is fluent and extremely efficient in tools of all different areas. For automation, tools like Jenkins and Bamboo are a must (3). All DevOps should exercise extensive knowledge in source code management tools, like Git. Software like Github and Bitbucket is important for a DevOp to sufficiently perform tasks with repository hosting. For containerization, a DevOp is expected to know Docker and Kubernetes well, just as they should know Puppet, Enterprise, Ansible, and Chef for configuration management (3). Tools to monitor software efficiently include Nagios and Raygun, and for project management your DevOp should be familiar with software solutions like Jira and Trello (3).
What Is DevOps? The Ultimate Guide (techtarget.com)

While DevOps will optimize and automate most if not all software testing, this is not their only function. DeVops are especially key, in their ability to software test (2). When running into a problem or needing to troubleshoot, the ability to manually test software is extremely handy. They have thorough understanding of diction and methodology, in the flow of software development. Successful DevOps know the importance of always looking for new ways to refine the development life cycle.

There’s a motivating philosophy, behind DevOp work. It walks a fine balance between two skills, expanding upon software development and IT operations. Additionally, the field of DeVops is always open to new players. Previous software engineers and IT staff who develop their skillset and cultivate a deep knowledge make excellent DevOps. Growing a multifaceted skillset is a foundational tenet for potential DevOps. They embrace opportunities to learn and continue fine-tuning themselves. Over the course of their careers, they develop good management, organization, and communication skills.

A DevOp is often the ultimate head manager of development projects, release dates, and sustainability within product updates. It is absolutely crucial they are efficient in management and organization. Schedules and team coordination will be primary concerns for a DevOp. Thus, they must also be friendly and well-versed communicators. The most efficient and organized manager cannot improve coordination within a team, if they are not an excellent communicator themselves. In a world growing faster in pace by the second, the contributions of a DevOp are not merely a luxury. They are an absolute requirement. By merging a developer's need to introduce new features and an IT operator's need to preserve stability, DevOps create seamlessness within any software project.

title: Looking into the Future: Bionic Eyes
paragraphs: Human biology is a finicky thing to maintain. However, emerging biotechnologies will hopefully help improve quality of life. The field of bionics looks promising, keeping technology and humanity closely intertwined. An exciting recent development in biotech surrounds bionic vision.
New Brain Implant Lets Blind Patient See Without Eyes (futurism.com)

Spanish researchers from Miguel Hernández University developed a brain implant to enhance vision in the visually impaired (1). At a length of 1.5 mm and a width of 4 mm, the current device consists of a “three-dimensional matrix of 96 micro-electrodes” (1). The implant is also connected to a camera, allowing it to process light signals and send them as feedback to the electrodes. Finally, these electrodes interact with neurons within the brain tissue. The device was first tested on primates, to strong success. The researchers then conducted studies with the help of a 57-year-old woman, who had been blind for 16 years (1). The implant was carefully placed along the visual cortex of her brain.

Despite the system containing several components, the researchers reported a low power draw on their device when compared to similar systems (2). Furthermore, studies showed that the only neurons affected by the electrodes were the target neurons, with neurons outside of the visual cortex being unresponsive to the electrical signals (2). However, the most reassuring data from the research was that the visual apparatus allowed the woman to identify letters, and various other “shape boundaries” (2) . More volunteers for the technology are currently being recruited, and outlook on its development is promising.

Seeing where technology is going can be a difficult task. Bionic vision technology may very well be a next step in biomedical technology. That said, depending on how the research develops, it just as easily may be a dead end. In either case, the research is bound to provide us knowledge that is of value. New technologies and innovations allow us to make the lives of others better. Thus, when this goal is at the forefront of scientific efforts, it is always a good sign.

title: Restaurant Robots: Computerized Chefs
paragraphs: The Age of Robotics is upon us. While this leaves a sour taste in the mouths of many, corporations and roboticists are working as hard as they can to change this. Literally. Several corporations are rolling out restaurant robots, that can both cook food and serve the customer. Despite the mixed feelings that will undoubtedly surround this topic, this change is hopefully a sign of great things to come for automation.
Restaurants looking for labor and speed turn to robots (cnbc.com)

Labor shortages are becoming widespread, particularly for minimum wage jobs. 4 out of 5 restaurants are reported as being understaffed (1). In the wake of this, several companies are looking to automation to resolve their woes. Recently, Miso Robotics introduced a restaurant robot known as “Flippy” (1). It is a high-precision robotic arm, capable of producing and cooking various foods. While it is currently at the high price-point of $20,000 (1), several large chains have already adopted it for testing. Once fully integrated, it will likely be worth the price. It has been reported that the robots allow workers to better interact with customers and provide good customer service.
A Florida restaurant chain says staff got bigger tips after it hired a $1,000-a-month robot to carry plates (yahoo.com)

Following suit, the company Softbank released a robot called the “Servi Robot”. It has already undergone testing and data analysis at the Sergio chain. They report an increase in tips for their waiters, and an increase of 25-30% for waiter efficiency. What makes the Servi Robot particularly unique is that it can handle the labor-intensive aspects of a waiter, allowing a waiter to focus more on maintaining the customer experience. Retrofitted with cameras, laser sensors, and a touchscreen, it can cleanly navigate a restaurant space. Thus, the server bot is capable of carrying out transactions, serving meals, and carrying back dirty dishes. Furthermore, it is extremely cost effective, only coming at a cost of $1,000 a month if a restaurant wants to rent it out.

Robots are the pinnacle of current human technology, combining electronics, computer science, and mechanics into a machine that can mimic life itself. Thus, in some ways, the decision to use robots to make fast food is disappointing. Nevertheless, big things always start small. Robotic waiters are a business model that is beginning to prove itself, and makes sense all-around. This is a strong sign that large shifts are about to occur for human society as a whole.

title: A Bit on the Tesla Bot
paragraphs: Elon Musk is infamous for his flashy announcements, on new tech. The recent announcement of Tesla Bot at Elon Musk’s AI day is no exception. In many ways, the announcement was gimmicky, and more flash than substance. Nevertheless, if the Tesla Bot can be delivered to the specifications that were promised, it has a ton of potential. It is truly a sign of how far innovation has come.
Tesla Bot - Tesla Bot: Elon Musk Reveals Humanoid Tesla Robot Which Is Apparently Not A Joke (forbes.com)

The Tesla Bot announcement was primarily concepts, with no prototype to be shown. The concept art featured a sleek, humanoid design, unlike more mechanized robots from companies like Boston Dynamics. Much of this is due to the proposed motor systems that the Tesla Bot will be using. Rather than relying on pneumatics, like Boston Dynamics, it will purely rely on electromechanical actuators (1). 40 electromechanical actuators have been announced, in total, according to Forbes: “12 in the arms, two each in the neck and torso, 12 in the legs, and 12 in the hands” (1). Due to the Tesla Bot’s proposed purpose being industrial (2), rather than for military use, it can also afford the reduction in power that electromechanical motors may create.

While Tesla Bot’s power source remains undisclosed, its proposed raw power is still nothing to scoff at. Supposedly, the robot will be able to lift 45lbs, and deadlift 150lbs (2). Moreover, it will hold this power in a small package, weighing only 125lbs and having a height of 5’8” (2).

Intimidating as the Tesla Bot may sound, the design intent is for it to be friendly to interact with. It will feature a touch screen for its face, allowing for smooth user input and interaction (1). Additionally, it will only be able to achieve speeds of 5 mph, and should be able to easily be overpowered (1). As Elon Musk put it, “We’re setting it such that it is at a mechanical level, a physical level, that you can run away from it, and most likely overpower it” (1).

When it comes to Elon Musk, it pays to take his announcements with a healthy dose of skepticism. In the same announcement panel, a person dressed in a pajama jumpsuit was used as an example of how the Tesla Bot may perform movement. Oftentimes, the products Musk winds up delivering pale in comparison to the products that he initially announced. Nevertheless, humanoid robots like the proposed Tesla Bot are technologies that have potential to become world changing. Whether Musk or another company are the first to deliver on such robots remains to be seen. In any case, humanoid robots are likely to become commonplace in the not-so-distant future. One can only hope that the people at Tesla can manage to pull their vision off.

title: Terraforming Earth with Sulfur
paragraphs: Humanity has been operating something of an experiment over the past few decades, with its wild emissions of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere. The globe has been rising in temperature levels at an exponential rate, and the trends are only expected to continue. Terraforming the earth via stratospheric sulfur injections is a proposed solution, to cool the Earth as carbon emissions heat it up. We may be able to stop global warming in a similar process that we used to create it.

While clean energy solutions have been proposed to stave off carbon emissions, they have thus far not reached the scale required to so. Carbon emissions show little sign of slowing down. If clean energy initiatives fail to overcome carbon emissions, sulfur injection may be the necessary next step. Sulfur aerosols would be pumped into the stratosphere, scattering radiation so that less radiation reaches the troposphere. Since the troposphere is where the bulk of the Earth’s weather phenomena occurs, this would mean a cooler Earth (1). The benefits of sulfur injections would be widespread. Polar ice caps would cease to melt. Plants would take in more CO2, causing stronger growth.

While methods of sulfur injections have not been tested on mass scale, an example of this concept was the eruption of Mount Pinatubo in 1991, which cooled the Earth by half a degree over several years (1). Furthermore, some scientists and inventors have tried and failed at patents and small scale experiments. The most notable attempt was from 2009, where a group of Russian scientists sprayed aerosols from a helicopter 200 meters up and reported reduced sunlight on the surface (3). While sulfur injections have potential, it is important to be skeptical toward proposed methods of implementation.

There are flaws to the idea of using sulfur geoengineering to solve the climate crisis. Sulfur being in the stratosphere would leave the sky a dull gray, removing the blue sky (2). There is also potential for satellite signal interference, ozone depletion, and reduction in efficiency of solar energy production (2). Sulfur would also only enable humanity to accelerate carbon production. Due to increasingly excess carbon in the atmosphere, halting sulfur emissions into the stratosphere would cause a catastrophic acceleration in the rate of global warming, 5-10 times what we currently see (2). Furthermore, while sulfur might work to cool down the Earth, it would do little to address the issues of deforestation, pollution, and damage to ocean life.

There are no clean answers to the climate crisis, and all possible solutions must be taken into account. While there is likelihood that clean energy solutions may be the way of escape, it is possible that a drastic measure like sulfur injection may be necessary in the coming future. While not an ideal solution, it is still solution that is able to cool the Earth down. It should be pursued, especially for an eventuality in which all other options have been exhausted.

title: Fusion and its Future
paragraphs: Renewable energy is one of the most important causes that is being worked on. However, a form of renewable energy sources that has yet to pan out is fusion energy. While fusion makes sense theoretically, there are practical challenges with fusion that have yet to be solved.
HL-2M Reactor - Nuclear Fusion At 100: The Hidden Race For Energy Supremacy | Hackaday

The way that fusion works is by harnessing the energy produced in the fusing of two atoms to form one (1). A massive benefit of fusion is that, unlike the radioactive products of nuclear fission, fusion does not produce radioactive waste as a product of the reaction. Rather, in addition to its energy output, it produces the useful element of helium. The general reactions being researched are between tritium (a hydrogen isotope with two neutrons and one proton) and deuterium (a hydrogen isotope with one proton and one neutron), due to reactions like deuterium-deuterium being untenable with current technology (1). Fusion limitations derive from the absence of a starlike gravity to compress atoms together. The temperatures required to overcome the atomic repulsion in fusion reactions are about 100 million Kelvin; this is six times hotter than the Sun’s core. In addition to extreme temperatures, atoms must be bombarded with ion particles, magnetic fields, lasers, and microwaves (1). All this energy input is what causes difficulty in getting a positive energy output.

There are several designs that have been tested for fusion, such as z-pinch reactors and stellarator reactors. However, the primary design that is widely being funded by world governments is the tokamak. The tokamak is a donut of magnets, cryo-pumps, and energy redirection systems known as “diverters”, surrounding a reactor core. With the help of Lorentz force, they contort a magnetic field to a helix, with the intent of directing fusion plasma into a steady flow (2). The two fusion reactors of this breed that are currently being tested are China’s HL-2M tokomak and Germany’s W-X7 tokomak, which were put into operation in 2020. Further tests on these reactors throughout the 2020s will hopefully reveal new information on how to optimize the fusion process, and bring us closer to fusion with net energy gain.
Tokomak Magnet Design - Nuclear Fusion At 100: The Hidden Race For Energy Supremacy | Hackaday

In addition to massive fusion reactors, several other types of fusion have been theorized. These include cold fusion, and compact fusion reactors. Though, a common thread through all fusion reactors is that they have experimentally only achieved a net zero output of energy. One of the most famous examples of this is the ITER. This fusion reactor is claimed to produce ten times its energy input but, in practical application, it operates quite different. The design is projected to convert 150 megawatts from the electrical grid to 50 megawatts of power to start the reactor. It will then convert 50 megawatts of reactor start power into 500 megawatts of plasma power, and convert 500 megawatts of plasma power into 150 megawatts of power to go back into the electrical grid (3). More simply put, the reactor will take 150 megawatts in, and spit 150 megawatts out. A net zero output is quite a bit less than an output that is “ten times the input”.

Complex and entrancing as the fusion process is, current fusion reactors are functionally no different from a metal wire.  While mere speculation, it is possible that there is a fundamental flaw on a thermodynamic level with trying to reproduce fusion at small scales. Perhaps a net energy gain from the reaction is unachievable, without the advantage of a starlike gravitational pull to motivate it.

The concept of clean reactors producing energy for the world is a beautiful one, and difficult to let go of. Fundamentally, the science is sound; fusion from stars in the sky are constant proof that fusion does work, and on mass scale. If there is a way to make fusion reactors become successful, it is worth it to continue trying. Thus, some of the brightest minds in science are chipping away at the problem, with the hopes of cracking it. Though, whether their intellectual challenge to make fusion successful has potential, or is merely the modern equivalent of Isaac Newton chasing the “philosopher’s stone”, remains to be seen.

title: Unpacking Jet-Packs
paragraphs: Flight technology is one of the greatest achievements of humanity. Nevertheless, no technology is ever finished. Jetpacks that allow people to journey through the sky have long been a dream of inventors. Thus, jetpack technologies are in constant development. It is quite possible that jetpacks will one day be used by emergency response teams and military personnel. Though, there are fundamental issues with jetpack technologies, which have yet to be overcome.

The fundamental way in which most jetpacks work is by using fuel to generate thrust, via jet engines. This requires implementation of heavy-duty jet fuel and jet engines, which are also compact (for more about how jet engines work, see here). They also have on-board engine computers, which are used to optimize flight control and stabilization. Unfortunately, due to the limited energy density of jet fuel, jetpacks are generally optimized between a half a minute and a minute of flight time (1). Jet-packs are excellent at achieving massive heights, in short spans of time, but they are unable to sustain their heights.
The Martin Jetpack (newatlas.com)

Despite the limitations of conventional jetpack technologies, ducted fan technologies have been tested and have proven more viable. Martin Aircraft, which has since gone under, produced a flight pack from a petrol engine and ducted fans. It was capable of 30 minutes of flight time and achieving a height of over 8,000 feet (2). The primary flaw in the company was that they initially claimed they would sell their technology to private consumers, at a cost of $86,000. It is likely that, if they had been consistent in their business model and sought investment from military contractors, they would still be around today.

Outside of using petrol engines to power ducted fans, there are theoretical also talks of using electric brushless motors. In simple terms, these would be ducted drone propellers that could be worn around the human body. Currently, there is a limitation from doing this, due to power constraints caused by the density of lithium-ion batteries.  Though, advancements in battery technology would quickly change this. Thankfully, the military and private industry alike are desperate to find such a miracle battery.

Concerning the future of conventional jetpack, advancements are still being made. Companies like Gravity Industries and JetPack Aviation are each private companies that also are currently pushing the edges of jetpack technology.

Due humans being inherently flightless, the challenge of producing an efficient jetpack is immense. Despite this, jetpacks do exist, and they are becoming better by the year. It is quite likely that, in the not-too-distant future, we will see battery technology give rise to jetpacks in much the same way that battery advancements gave rise to the electric car. Just, don’t expect to ever see your neighbor flying one of them.

title: Solar Panels: The Generation of Regeneration
paragraphs: One of the greatest threats to our civilization is ourselves. More specifically, it is the carbon emissions that we generate. In all fairness to ourselves, immense carbon generation is only to expected from a society of carbon-based lifeforms. Nevertheless, regenerative technologies are the way of the future, with the potential of bringing us to carbon neutrality. Solar energy, in the form of solar panels, is an essential piece of this.

The function of solar panels is to harness energy from the Sun. Specifically, it harnesses photonic energy by having photons knock electrons from its solar cells. This knocking of electrons creates an electric polarization; more precisely, electric charge in the form of electricity. The material used in solar cells to accomplish this is generally a thin film of silicon atoms, due to its accessibility (1). Though, there are rarer metals that could give a better performance than silicon (namely, tungsten). The solar cell film is placed between polarized material meshes to encourage a buildup of charge. These materials are boron for a positive charge and phosphorous for a negative charge (1). There are also conductive metal wires along the solar cells, to transmit resulting electricity. Finally, there is glass plating overtop solar panels, to contain photonic energy and protect the solar cells.

Advances in solar cells are continual. Currently, researchers have achieved silicon films that are as thin as 1.3 microns. Other forms of solar power technology are also being developed, such as concentrated solar power and thermal solar power, which stand to have higher energy efficiency (1). Due to the silicon being second to oxygen as the Earth’s most abundant molecule, and solar panels having relatively minimal issues on the environment, these advancements are unlikely to stop any time soon.
Solar Panels - How Do Solar Panels Work? (gizmodo.com.au)

Solar energy is spreading throughout the world as a wildfire. They are being installed five times faster than coal power stations, and twenty times faster than nuclear power stations. In Australia, new power production facilities are exclusively solar or wind farms. Australia’s new initiative also comes with good reason, as sunlight from the Sun on their land potentially has 20,000 times the energy as the USA is able to produce from gas, oil, and coal (2). Due to technological advancements and government regulations, solar cells have gotten cheaper to produce by 99% since the 1980s (3).

While work is still to be done to make solar cells more effective at energy production, solar technology has already come a long way from where it was during its inception. Renewable energy only stands to grow, as the globe becomes more heated from immense carbon emissions. Solar panels are not the entire solution to the energy question, but they are an integral part of it.

title: LEDS vs. Incandescent Lightbulbs: Shedding a Light on the Difference
paragraphs: The lightbulb is a crown jewel of invention, commonly credited to Edison and his company of General Electric. However, the lightbulbs that we use today are quite different than the lightbulbs of yesteryear. GE’s original lightbulb was of the incandescent variety. Though, the lightbulbs mostly used today are actually LED lightbulbs.
LED Lightbulbs - Difference Between LED and Incandescent | Difference Between

The way that incandescent lightbulbs work is by flowing electricity through a tungsten filament, causing the filament to give off a warm glow. Generally, lightbulbs are filled with an inert gas (oxygen would enflame) and heated to up 2200 degrees centigrade (1). Meanwhile, Light Emitting Diodes (LEDs) work from an electric circuit, which sends charged electrons between a cathode and anode through a semiconductor. The semiconductor is generally made of aluminum-gallium-arsenide. This electrical circuit concentrates electrical energy and gives off the electroluminescent glow needed to light up a room.

While there is a certain charm and nostalgia about the concept of incandescent lightbulbs, LED lights are vastly superior. Firstly, incandescent lights have the shortest lifespans of any lighting system. Standard incandescent lights only last for 1,000 to 2,000 hours. Meanwhile, LED lights are estimated to have 25,000 to 30,000 hours of lifespan (1). A more important factor is energy efficiency. Incandescent bulbs waste 90% of the energy they use as heat, whereas LED lighting systems use 35 to 80% of their energy for lighting (1). While LED lightbulbs tend to cost a bit more than incandescent bulbs, the investment is more than worth it. In the long run, this amounts to massive energy savings.

The advantages of LEDs don’t stop here, however. LEDs are also mercury free, unlike incandescent bulbs (2). Incandescent bulbs have continuous flickering as well, due to gas movement, while LEDs produce a continuous flow of light (2). Finally, LEDs have far more control than incandescent bulbs. Depending on the lightbulb, one can easily alter the directionality, color, and brightness of the light.

Plenty of homes still have incandescent lights. Though, it is worth considering making the transition to LEDs. Their clever design will help improve the environment, one’s living space, and one’s wallet. In every respect, LEDs are the superior technology.

title: Breaking Down Regenerative Braking
paragraphs: Carbon emissions are a hot button topic, due to the accelerating pace of global warming. One of the places we need to reverse carbon emissions from is cars. New automotive technologies have been introduced, such as hybrid and electric engines, to combat emissions. Within hybrid and electric cars, there is also a prominent form of braking: regenerative braking. It is an incredibly useful technology, which will be around for years to come.
What Is Regenerative Braking? | News | Cars.com

Regenerative braking takes advantage of kinetic energy, rather than solely relying on the friction braking of mechanical systems. Specifically, as an electric or hybrid car brakes, regenerative braking sends the car wheels’ rotational motion into its electrical motors. The electrical motors are reversed, thus acting as a miniature electrical generator and adding energy back into the car. Mechanical braking rotors are not used in these systems until the very last moments of braking.

While its surge in usage is new, regenerative braking is a concept that has been around for over a hundred years, in things like trolleys, trains, and electric cars (1). These systems make up a good portion of the energy efficiency of electric and hybrid cars, by saving the heat energy that a mechanical braking system would otherwise take. It is estimated that 70% of a car’s kinetic energy is recaptured from regenerative braking. In hybrid cars, this can lead to a 25-45% reduction in fuel usage. As time has progressed, regenerative braking systems have also become smoother than mechanical braking systems. The electrical motors of hybrid and electric cars are controlled by a series of circuits, which monitor a car’s rotational motion to bring it to a smooth stop (3). A final advantage of regenerative braking systems is that they do not wear out as quickly. This is since, rather than relying on the brute friction of brake rotors for stopping, regenerative brakes are redirecting motion into stopping energy.

Ingenious as classical mechanical braking systems are, regenerative braking systems are a step above. Their large energy savings, smoothness of use, and enhanced durability make them vastly superior to pure mechanical systems. While mechanical braking systems will remain a common component to gasoline cars, electrical and hybrid cars are becoming more commonplace. As this trend continues, regenerative braking is likely to become an industry standard.
By: Christian Mueth

title: The Facts on Vaccination
paragraphs: Vaccines are a miracle of medical technology, allowing humanity to combat diseases that would otherwise be devastating. New COVID-19 vaccines are especially valuable, offering a chance to end the COVID-19 pandemic. These vaccines are the product of tireless work from scientists and researchers. Yet, with the recent vaccine breakthroughs, there is also backlash. According to a poll from Pew Research Center, 39% of people say they will not be receiving the vaccine (2). An unfounded undercurrent of fear regarding COVID-19 vaccines has emerged, and it is important to be informed on the facts of COVID-19 vaccines’ importance.
How do mRNA vaccines work – and why do you need a second dose? 5 essential reads (yahoo.com)

The first misconception to address is the idea that the COVID-19 vaccines are untested. While it is true that COVID-19 vaccines are being rolled out faster than usual, they have also undergone intense scrutiny to make sure they meet safety standards. This includes a four-stage approval process from the FDA, an approval from the EUA, and an approval from the CDC (1). Currently, the CDC is monitoring for any potentially serious risks and side effects, but none have been found thus far (1). Many have already received the vaccine, such as those in emergency and medical fields.

The way that the Pfizer and Moderna vaccines work is via a unique technique. They send mRNA into the body, which tells the cells to produce some of the proteins produced by the COVID-19 virus. The immune system recognizes these proteins as foreign and develops an immune response to them (2). Essentially, this means that only a small portion of the COVID-19 virus’ DNA needed to be used in vaccines, rather than the entire pathogen. However, this also means that the vaccine has to be given in two doses. The first dose primes the body’s immune system, and the second dose is what grants true immunity (3). New data collection processes were used, and world governments collaborated, for the expedient development of these vaccines (1).

While the vaccines are safe to use, there are some minor side effects that are to be made known. 70% of those who have taken the vaccine report pain in their arm, according to a survey of 2 million people from the CDC (1). Less than a third of people also have reports of tiredness, headaches, and nausea (1). These symptoms are minor, but noteworthy all the same. The larger difficulty facing the COVID-19 vaccines has to do with means of delivery. They must be stored in subzero temperatures, to prevent spoiling of the mRNA material (3). Thus, there is a vast supply chain being developed, to properly preserve the vaccines.

COVID-19 is an advent in history that will never be forgotten. How we choose to move forward will forever set the precedent for how pandemics like this will be handled in the future. While the idea of getting a shot is never comfortable, in times like these we need to put aside what is comfortable and trust in the broader scientific process.

title: SpaceX Starlink: Internet for the Masses
paragraphs: SpaceX recently came crashing onto headlines with yet another test flight crash of the Starship 9. Nevertheless, SpaceX has recently found success in a different arena: satellites. SpaceX recently successfully launched thousands of satellites into space, for their new Starlink internet service. They now own approximately a third of all active satellites in the sky (1). As one might imagine from SpaceX, this move is both controversial and game changing.
SpaceX plans to boost Starlink network with launch - UPI.com

SpaceX’s satellite web consists of 1,000 satellites orbiting 340 miles above the Earth, with the plan of eventually reaching 40,000 satellites (1). The objective of the satellite service is to beam cheap, highspeed internet to rural areas, where internet is often spotty or limited. Already, they have 10,000 customers (1). Already, it has proven a success among those that use it. At a price tag of $99 a month, users have reported that the service is significantly better than most local offerings. Elon Musk, SpaceX’s CEO, has projected the service to provide $30 billion a year for the company. This would be ten times more than their usual rocketry revenue streams — a major source of funding for their ultimate missions to Mars.

While the future of Starlink looks bright, its bright future may also pose a problem. Many astronomers have expressed concerns of light pollution from the satellites (1). Satellites have already interfered with several telescope images, requiring astronomers to do more work when parsing through their data. Furthermore, there are increased fears of collisions with space debris. SpaceX has attempted to address these concerns by keeping their satellites in low orbit and using sun visors (1). Though, it is likely that ground based observatories are on their way out due to these shifts.

On top of space concerns, there are economic concerns. While Starlink is only $99 monthly, it requires a $499 deposit for the compatible equipment (2). Additionally, SpaceX had to take out massive loans to fund this project (2). Starlink is also facing competition from many other services. Blue Origin plans to start a satellite network known as Kuiper, and there are also the networks of OneWeb and Telesat (2). Elon Musk himself has even acknowledged the ambitiousness on the project. Specifically, he had this to say: “Every new satellite constellation in history has gone bankrupt. We hope to be the first that does not” (3).

Considering the track record of SpaceX, it is safe to assume that this service is in position to be yet another massive win for the company. Risky as many of their moves are, they always are moving toward the future. There is high probability that satellite networks like Starlink are on their way to becoming a standard usage throughout the world’s rural communities.

title: The Science Behind Quantum ComputersIBM is aiming for 'frictionless' quantum computing by 2025 - Compsmag
paragraphs: Our world is dominated by computers small enough to fit in a pocket. Though, a new form of computing called “quantum computing” is on the rise. Moore’s law (an annual doubling of computing density) is beginning to wane, as humanity reaches the physical limits of classical computing. Quantum computing stands to reaccelerate computing advancement. It will bring a major shift in how computing works and technological capabilities never seen before.
IBM promises 100x faster quantum computers through new software foundations (msn.com)

Classical computing works off a logical system called “binary”. Transistors provide the computer outputs of 1s and 0s, known as “bits”, which are read as true or false statements. This logical system is fundamental to all computer technology we see today. Yet, quantum computing uses a concept that is stranger and more efficient, by more than just a bit. Quantum computers leverage the physics of subatomic particles, known as quantum physics, to read “qubits”. Qubits, rather than holding one of two positions like bits, are capable of superposition. Simply put, qubits can hold a range of various states all at once (1). Qubits can also become entangled with other qubits, forming a multidimensional processing network (1). This allows quantum computers to solve problems in a lateral fashion, where different possibilities are considered at the same time.

Quantum computing is in position to overhaul multiple industries. Physics simulations, chemical compositions, genetic sequences, material structures, and more will be easily processed by quantum computers. Quantum computers will arrive at solutions that are faster and better than anything classical computers can provide (1). Furthermore, the fields of machine learning and artificial intelligence will vastly increase in performance (1). A big ongoing test of quantum computing’s problem-solving ability regards trade. Exxon has teamed up with IBM to optimize shipping networks through quantum computing (2).

Currently, all major tech companies invest heavily into quantum computing, with Google, Intel, Microsoft, and IBM being among them. IBM is the current industry leader, looking to make the jump from a 27 qubit computer to a 1121 qubit computer (3). They are making their software and supply chain open source, to allow for easy parallel development throughout industry (3). The current hope of IBM is that quantum computing will be “frictionless” for developers by 2025 (4).

Despite the advantages of quantum computing, there are cold realities that must be faced. Due to the experimental nature of the technology, results are largely inconsistent. It is estimated by industry experts that it may be 5 to 10 years before consistent results are reached (1). Additionally, quantum computers require extreme conditions to operate. They are kept at a cold .015 degrees Kelvin (nearly absolute zero) and must be shielded up to 50,000 times the Earth’s magnetic field (1). Due to these factors, quantum computers are more likely to be rented out as a service than sold as industrial machines; let alone be sold for personal use.

It is quite possible that quantum computers still have a long road ahead and are decades away from reaching peak performance. This was much the case for classical computers, with them taking decades to truly advance. Yet, quantum computers are a future reality, whether that future comes sooner or later. Furthermore, whatever future reality quantum computers exist in, it will be quite unlike anything we see today.

title: Hydroelectric Dams
paragraphs: With the spiraling state of the world’s climate, renewable energy resources are a must. One of the biggest producers of renewable energy today are hydroelectric dams. However, the specifics of their mechanisms are lost to many. Moreover, while hydroelectric dams have their benefits, there are also drawbacks that are often overlooked. Exploring the details of hydroelectric dams is intriguing, and well worth it.
OPG completes rehab of reservoir at 174-MW Sir Adam Beck Pump Generating Station - Hydro Review

At their core, hydroelectric dams take energy from the flow of a body of water, and convert it into electricity. However, a key condition is that the body of water sees a large drop in elevation. This is because hydroelectric dams depend on the potential energy from gravity that water holds. There are also several stages to the energy production process. First, water from the body of water gets stored in a large reservoir. Following this, water is let through a gate called a “sluice gate” (1). It then falls through a channel called a “penstock”, and its kinetic energy is used to turn a generator. The generator produces this electrical energy by generating an electrical field, from its magnetic copper coils. The electrical energy is finally sent from the generator to a transformer, which sends the electricity to the electrical grid, and to the wider populous. Meanwhile, all the water that passes through the generator is released to the downstream.
Hydroelectric Power: How it Works (usgs.gov)

One of the big advantages of hydroelectric dams is that they are amazing at giving big bursts of electricity when there is high demand. This is because they can store water in their reservoir, and release to generate electricity as needed. Its function is like that of a massive battery (1). An example of when quick power generation might be of use would be during a massive summer heatwave. Additionally, they’re incredibly efficient, accounting for 20% of the world’s energy production (3). The efficiency of a hydroelectric plant is defined by its flow and head (2). Flow is the amount of water that flows through the generator. Head is the distance that the water will drop before hitting the generator and is where the bulk of the kinetic energy comes from. Because of these two factors, the electricity that hydroelectric dams produce gives less emissions and is substantially cheaper than that of, say, thermal power plants (3).

The biggest drawback of hydroelectric dams is that they impose massive changes on the surrounding ecosystem. Populations of fish and surrounding fauna often are driven away or reduced in number. Citizens living near the construction sites of hydroelectric dams are also often forced to relocate. Furthermore, while hydroelectric dams give less emissions than other forms of power plants, they still release methane into the atmosphere, due to the standing body of water that they hold in their reservoir (2).

Limitations exist for the hydroelectric dam, decreasing their prevalence. Nevertheless, where they are successful, they provide massive benefits. Hydroelectric dams may be a complicated technology, but it is their complexity that contributes to the simple conveniences of modern society.

title: A Description of Cryptocurrency
paragraphs: The stock market exploded in 2017, as a new business model rose to prominence: cryptocurrency. Bitcoin was the main talk of the stock market, but other cryptocurrency companies were not far behind. The rise of cryptocurrency has added massive wealth for some, but financial burden for others. Despite the success of Bitcoin and its ilk, many cryptocurrency companies on the market are little more than Ponzi schemes. Some investors wonder whether the entire cryptocurrency craze is a bubble, waiting to burst. Navigating and understanding what cryptocurrency is, and how to be safe with it, is a difficult task. Due to the potential that cryptocurrency wields, it demands to be understood.

Cryptocurrency works by using virtual tokens (2) as a form of currency. One unique feature of cryptocurrency is that there is not a specific federal body that it is maintained by. The U.S. Dollar might have a Federal reserve to fall back on, but not so for a Bitcoin (1). Another difference is that cryptocurrencies are directly exchanged from person to person (1). Unlike money moved through banks or PayPal, there is no middleman. Bitcoin and its ilk also don’t have serial numbers to transactions for tracing back to the buyer or seller (1).

Despite the lack of conventional supervising bodies, cryptocurrency has a revolutionary system that ensures security. It uses blockchains, which are an encrypted database network. Better put, blockchains consist of countless blocks, that each store bits of data. In the case of cryptocurrency, blocks store transactional data. These blocks are arranged in a decentralized way, where blocks are given timestamps and added to a chain of blocks (3); the aforementioned “blockchain”. While every block stores its own data, it also acts as a node in the chain, and references information from other nodes to ensure its own accuracy (3). In cases where a node disagrees with the wider blockchain, it corrects itself (3). Thus, corruption of a cryptocurrency system would require corrupting most of a network’s decentralized nodes.

In addition to blockchains, cryptocurrencies have other provisions for secure transactions. Namely, they restrict and regulate user activity through public keys, private keys, proof of work, and proof of stake (2). A private key is a unique identification code, known only to a user, which allows a user to make transactions (2). A public key is used to verify private keys, during transactions (2). Proof of work is when computers run through an intense mathematical algorithm to verify a block’s legitimacy. Verifiers are rewarded with cryptocurrency. In proof of stake systems, verifiers stake part of their own cryptocurrency for a chance to verify blocks and earn more cryptocurrency (4). If a verifier verifies invalid transactions, verifiers lose out on more cryptocurrency, as well as a portion of their stake (4).

There are risks inherent to cryptocurrencies. Their reliance on technology means that there is no collateral in the event of system shutdowns or fraud (5). On the issue of fraud, there are many cyberthreats who create exchanges that are fake (5). The value of cryptocurrencies are turbulent, jumping from extreme highs to extreme lows (5). Finally, since cryptocurrencies are new, it is difficult to gauge what role they have. Many markets do not recognize cryptocurrencies, and many investors believe cryptocurrencies are vastly overvalued.

Cryptocurrency is complicated and involved. It also poses several issues. That said, it possesses many advantages, and will likely continue to gain ground as a legitimate form of currency. In the future, it might be just as ubiquitous as any form of federal currency.
By: Christian Mueth

title: Voting Machines: The Electronics Behind Elections
paragraphs: In the United States, another historic election has occurred. As such, there are many who have questions as to how our vote counting process operates. Specifically, people are turning a critical eye toward voting machines. There are questions regarding their reliability and security. Moreover, there is the larger looming question of what is going on underneath the hoods of our voting machines. Hopefully, in explaining how voting machines work, it can be better understood why they work.

Older voting machines were purely mechanical. Some worked by reading voter punch cards (1), whereas others worked by the pulling of a mechanical lever to indicate one’s vote (2). Today, most voting machines have followed in the footsteps of punch cards, using paper ballots to count votes. The reason for this has everything to do with transparency and security. If a machine is to mechanically fail, have software error, or be hacked, votes can still be recovered and recounted. An example of this happened in 2006 in Pottawattamie County; after a major machine error, election officials managed to do a proper hand count (1).

The way that modern voting machines read ballots is through digital imaging technology. With hand-marked ballots, when a voter fills out a bubble for a candidate and inserts it into a machine, the machine reads their filled in bubble. Following this, it will read a barcode on the side of a ballot, to work out the ballot’s coordinate map (3). Finally, it will use the ballot’s coordinate map to determine the bubble’s corresponding candidate and add it to the tally. In addition to hand-marked ballots, there are also machine marked ballots. A voter selects their candidate via touchscreen, and a prefilled ballot is printed out for them (3). Though, the following steps of the process work in much the same way as a hand-marked ballot. There is always a physical paper trail for the ballots, which can be reviewed.

In addition to a robust digital imaging system, there are other methods used to increase the efficacy of voting machines. Some ballot counting machines are capable of counting 800 ballots per minute (1). There are also automatic envelope openers and signature verification scanners for absentee ballots (1). Advancements have been made in voter registration systems, to keep better track of a voter’s proper ballot and precinct (2). Additionally, according to the political science professor Charles Stewart, “there’s a very large computer network that helps to aggregate all of those tallies, and to communicate them, at least unofficial tallies, to the press, to state election authorities” (2).

While voting machines are generally reliable, there are exceptions. One example would be “direct recording” machines; these machines use software to record what a voter enters on a touchscreen. There is no paper trail produced by these machines. The problem with this form of voting is that one must trust the software to reliably record what a voter puts in; once a vote is in, it is “impossible to audit” (1). It is estimated that 5% to 10% of voters use these machines (2). While they are being phased out in many places, and malfunctions are rare, they remain a potential issue for many voters.

Despite fears of cyberattacks and are rampant, they are unfounded. According to Mark Lindeman, co-director of verified voting, the biggest threats aren’t so much hackers as they are machine and human error. In his words, “To my knowledge, there is no verified report of a machine being hacked during an election. Definitely verified reports of machines malfunctioning, scanners being misprogrammed, etc., but nothing tying those to [a] cyberattack.”(4) The United States Homeland Security Secretary, Chad Wolf, echoes much the same thoughts, with “full confidence in the country’s voting infrastructure and no indications that it had been hacked” (4).

Every time there is an election, there is undoubtedly going to be doubt cast upon our voting process. Such doubt is to be expected and is even necessary. It is what keeps our election officials and voting system held accountable. Nevertheless, being able to have faith in our voting processes and voting technology is also important. Thankfully, on most counts, the process of counting votes appears to be fine and well.

title: Spot the Bot: The Future is a Lot Closer than Thought
paragraphs: Each day, it seems that robots make another step toward achieving world dominance. The incredible work coming out of Boston Dynamics is a prime example of this. Many have likely seen viral videos of their bipedal ATLAS robot, performing flips that would put an Olympian to shame. It is right on the cutting edge of technology. Yet, the most impressive creation coming out of Boston Dynamics right now isn’t their robotic gymnast. Rather, it is Spot. This four-legged robot is incredibly helpful, with uses in homes, public life, medical service, emergency service, and industry. Released only a year ago, on September 24th 2019 (1), it’s already changing the face of the robotics market.
https://www.engadget.com/boston-dynamics-will-start-selling-arms-for-its-robodog-spot-next-year-192343407.html

Before going into Spot’s practical applications, it helps to look at some of its capabilities. It has 360 degree cameras and sensors, it can move up to 3 miles per hour, it can carry a load of up to 30 pounds, it can deftly navigate harsh terrain, and it is resistant to water and dust (4). It is also highly trainable and programmable. In the coming year, Boston Dynamics also plans to provide separate parts for upgrades. These include a recharging pack for more range, a LIDAR pack for more precise sensing, and attachable robotic arm for increased dexterity (1).

Spot’s list of capabilities is exhaustive. Yet, Spot itself seems to be tireless in its applications. It has been used to “collect data and perform hazardous tasks” for manufacturing companies, such as Ford, BP, and Merck (3). A deal was also recently made for it to begin work on construction sites, for the company Trimble. Though, Spot’s most impressive uses are in regard to the recent COVID pandemic. It has been used in Brigham and Woman’s Hospital to take vitals of patients, and it is being used to help encourage social distancing in Singapore (3).

The list above paints a pretty picture for Spot. Yet, it’s still early in its life, and one may be wondering: where does the future of Spot seem to be headed? It is difficult to say. Earlier last year, Spot’s future was pitched to be in domestic, home entertainment (2). As recently as this year, Marc Raibert (Boston Dynamics founder) discussed the idea of Spot doing chores, such as somebody’s laundry (1). Currently though, the price point for Spot is extremely high — at 75,000$, no family will be buying one any time soon (1). It is worth noting that Boston Dynamics is known to get funding from America’s DOD. Additionally, only 300 robots have been produced (3), with all of them going toward industrial purposes. While Spot may one day be used as a home companion, seeing it on a manufacturing line, or helping to do menial public tasks, is far more likely.
https://qz.com/1635500/boston-dynamics-spot-may-be-used-as-a-battle-bot/

Spot’s legacy is still developing, but its influence on society is already immense. While cultural trends have suggested that robots are to play a large role in our future, Spot is cementing this. From its example, robots will become more commonplace in the workplace. We can expect to see them giving aid in heavy manual labor, and high-risk operations (i.e., rescue work, space travel). Perhaps this comes as no surprise; lest we forget, robots have already beaten humans to Mars. Though, Spot’s greater accomplishment is its friendly and efficient design. While it may easy to fear being replaced by an army of mindless automatons, Spot proves we should have nothing to fear. Robots are a major boost to progress and productivity. Spot is better being perceived as a companion pet, than a threat.
By: Christian Mueth
